result_text:
Tickets can now carry a support agent, and every ticket listing and the lookup by number return it. Unassigned tickets return null. The ticket tests pass, including a new one.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `support_ticket` has a new nullable `agent VARCHAR(100)` column. The agent is a free-text name, since the repo has no support-agent entity.
- **`model/SupportTicket.java`**: new `agent` component. A nine-argument constructor is kept so existing callers and tests still compile; it sets the agent to null.
- **`DataStore.java`**: the insert stores the agent. All eight ticket queries (customer, priority, region, sales rep, product, order, old high-priority region, open on date) and the lookup by number select and map `agent`. Status updates only touch `status` and `closed_date`, so the agent survives in progress and closing.
- **`service/SupportTicketService.java`**: new `create(number, customerId, orderNumber, agent, subject, priority, date)`. Blank agents are stored as null. The old six-argument `create` delegates with a null agent. `changeStatus` passes the agent through.
- **`SupportTicketTest.java`**: new `agentIsShownAndKeptOnStatusChange` test covering assigned and unassigned tickets across lists, status changes and lookup.

I ran the ticket-related test classes offline and they pass. I did not run the full suite.

I left `ClosedTicket` (the closed-tickets report) without an agent, since it isn't in your list. Say if you want it there too. Nothing is committed.
